title: The soul you gave me is pure
hookLine: Elohai Neshamah: my God, the soul you placed in me is pure

cards: What's the first thing your mind says to you in the morning? For some people it's a list of failures. You didn't finish that.
You said the wrong thing. You're behind. The inner critic is awake first.
Now set beside that the line the Talmud says to say on waking, before the blessings for eyes and legs and clothes. It doesn't begin with what you did wrong, or what you owe.
It begins with one word about who you are: pure.

teach.h: ELOHAI NESHAMAH: MY GOD, THE SOUL.
teach.b: The prayer is called Elohai neshamah, my God, the soul. In the Talmud, in Berakhot, it runs roughly like this: my God, the soul you placed in me is pure. You created it, you formed it, you breathed it into me.

You guard it within me, and one day you will take it from me, and return it in the time to come. As long as the soul is in me, I give thanks. And it ends: blessed are you, who restores souls to bodies.

Neshamah means soul, and it's close kin to the Hebrew word for breath. In Genesis, the old Jewish translation says God "breathed into his nostrils the breath of life." Breath of life there is nishmat chayim.
So you breathed it into me points back to the first human, and to every breath since. Notice the order.
Before thanks, before requests, before any confession, the prayer states: the soul is pure. Jewish teachers point to this line to say that each morning a person starts with a clean soul.
Mistakes are real, and the tradition takes repair very seriously. But the soul itself isn't the mistake. The prayer is honest about death too: one day the soul will be taken.
That's why waking is treated as a return.
In the prayer's telling, it was given back again this morning.

how: Elohai neshamah is said each morning among the morning blessings, at home or in the synagogue; many people also say the short Modeh Ani on first waking and Elohai neshamah after washing their hands.

games.why: the Talmud's waking prayer begins: my God, the soul you placed in me is pure. thanks and requests come after.

practice: Feel the air come in through your nose, cool, and go out, warm. Breathing in, think neshamah, breath and soul together; breathing out, say pure, aloud or inside.
If the critic starts its list, let it talk, and keep breathing under it.

carryVoice: Your line: the soul is pure. A week of the heart's work, the doorway, the dawn blessings, the rooster, opened eyes, strength for the weary, and a pure soul. Rest well.
